title: Ledger Conventions for Returning Money on a Keyturn Trip Booking
content:
Money is given back against one identified earlier line of a Keyturn Trip Booking and never against the reservation as a whole, so every refund names the charge line it reverses and the reversal can never exceed what that line took.

A line that has already been reversed in full is not reversed again, so where a refund line already stands against the same original charge and the earlier refund was not itself cancelled, the request is a duplicate and no further money moves.

A partial reversal is allowed where only part of the original line is in dispute, and several partial reversals against one original line are allowed as long as their total stays inside the original amount; each carries its own date and ground so that two partial reversals of the same amount remain separable.

The ground of the refund is recorded as given: a goodwill gesture, a host error, a marketplace error or a policy waiver, and the ground decides who ultimately bears the cost rather than whether the guest is made whole.

Refunds reach the guest's card within the plan's processing period counted in business days from the day the refund is posted, and the marketplace does not pay interest for that period.

Where the original line was taken from wallet credit rather than the card on file, the reversal returns wallet credit, because money is always returned by the route it arrived on.

### The duplicate condition

The question is settled on the reversal records already standing against the same original charge line, read before any further money moves and correlated to that original line's own reference. Where such a reversal already stands and has not itself been cancelled, and it gave back the whole of the original line, the request in front of the desk is a duplicate and no further money moves.

Two reversals against one original line are told apart by the date they were posted, the amount returned and the ground they were raised on. That is what allows two partial reversals of the same amount, raised on different days or on different grounds, to stand together.

### The grounds and what they decide

| Ground recorded | What it decides |
|---|---|
| A goodwill gesture | Who ultimately bears the cost. |
| A host error | Who ultimately bears the cost. |
| A marketplace error | Who ultimately bears the cost. |
| A policy waiver | Who ultimately bears the cost. |

None of the four grounds changes whether the guest is made whole; each decides where the cost finally falls.

### Two boundaries on the amount

*Hypothetical.* An original line of 90.00 USD has already been reversed by 30.00 USD on one ground and 25.00 USD on another. A further reversal of 35.00 USD stays inside the original amount, since the three together come to 90.00 USD; a further reversal of 40.00 USD would take the total past the original line and cannot be raised, because a reversal can never exceed what the line it names took.

### The route the money takes

Where the original line was taken from the card on file, the reversal reaches that card within the plan's processing period, counted in business days from the day the refund is posted. Where the original line was taken from wallet credit, the reversal returns wallet credit.
